title: Hindalco Industries Ltd - 500440 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Hindalco Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT fell 51% to INR2,597 crore on Oswego fire, but adjusted PAT rose 10% to INR5,796 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated business-segment EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR10,812 crore, while reported PAT fell 51% to INR2,597 crore due to exceptional items including the Novelis Oswego plant fire. India business segment EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR6,610 crore and PAT rose 11% to INR3,549 crore. Copper EBITDA hit a record INR907 crore on higher by-product (sulfuric acid) realisations, while Novelis adjusted EBITDA was about $498 million ($543/t). Management expects Novelis to recover in FY27 as Oswego hot mill restarts and Bay Minette ramps.

segments.name: India aluminium upstream
segments.commentary: Shipments +2% YoY, revenue +11% YoY, EBITDA INR5,448 crore at $1,756/t. Q4 cost rose about 2.4% QoQ; Q1 FY27 guided about 5% higher, mainly furnace oil.

segments.name: India aluminium downstream
segments.commentary: Shipments 124 KT (+18% YoY), EBITDA INR255 crore (+16% YoY), $226/t, driven by volume, mix and premiumisation.

segments.name: Copper (India)
segments.commentary: Record EBITDA INR907 crore (+48% YoY) on by-product realisations and efficiencies; metal shipments 128 KT (-5%), CCR volumes 91 KT (+11%).

segments.name: Novelis
segments.commentary: Shipments 917 KT (-4% YoY) excluding 73 KT Oswego loss; adjusted EBITDA $498 million ($543/t). Impacts: $53 million Oswego fire, $27 million tariffs, offset by $41 million Sierre flood insurance recovery.

guidance_outlook: Novelis: Oswego hot mill to restart in the next few weeks; current-year headwinds expected to substantially recover in FY27; long-term $600/t EBITDA target intact.
Novelis cost programme: FY26 exit run-rate savings raised to $200 million (from $125 million target); 3-year structural cost cut of $350-400 million by FY28 exit.

Novelis Bay Minette 600 KT greenfield plant: cold mill commissioning started, hot mill commissioning from next month, commercial coils in FY28, 18-24 month ramp; start-up costs of about $100-150 million annually expected below EBITDA.
India copper TC/RCs: more than 85% contracted at benchmark; expected close to zero or slightly negative for FY27.
India copper EBITDA: Q1 FY27 similar to Q4 (INR900 crore range) but management guided INR600-700 crore per quarter for Q2 and Q3.

India capex FY27 about INR12,000 crore (later framed as INR15,000-17,000 crore for the next year); Novelis FY27 capex $2.3-2.4 billion, mainly Bay Minette; consolidated net debt peak INR80,000-90,000 crore over next 2 years; net leverage around 2x.
Aluminium market: deficit now 1.5 million t for CY26 (from 0.3 million t), tightest in Q2-Q3 CY26.
Renewable capacity 470 MW at year end, rising to 523 MW by end Q1 FY27.
capex_capacity: Aditya smelter: first 180 pots by December 2027, next 180 pots by December 2028; management says timelines look firm.

Captive coal: Chakla box cut expected in next 2 months, first coal possibly Q4 FY27; Bandha box cut done but first coal only in FY28 due to high strip ratio; Meenakshi (strip ratio under 1) expected to add substantial volumes in FY29; Chakla Stage 1 forest clearance received.

Downstream: Aditya FRP ramping up; battery enclosure at full ramp-up; Aditya battery foil commissioned; Taloja AC fin facility commissioning; specialty alumina precipitate hydrate commissioned, under customer approval.

Copper: inner grooved tubes (35 KT) in customer qualification; 50 KT Pakhajan e-waste recycling plant to commission in August; copper smelter about 3 years out; battery grade copper foil scaled down to a smaller capacity in about 2 years.
demand_pricing: Aluminium prices strengthened in the quarter; West Asia conflict disrupted supply; global market now seen in 1.5 million t deficit for CY26.
India Q4 FY26 aluminium demand about 1.6 million t, +9% YoY; India copper demand 402 KT, +10% YoY.
Q4 FY26 hedges: aluminium 64% at INR2,807/t; currency 26% at INR88/$. FY27 hedges: aluminium 29% at $3,013/t; currency 14% at INR90.13/$.
Sulfuric acid prices high due to Middle East conflict and China export restrictions; management expects Q1 FY27 to be slightly above Q4 but could correct if Strait of Hormuz reopens.
Global concentrate TC/RCs at record lows around -$0.21 to -$0.25/lb; expected to stay negative through FY27.
Alumina sales 211 KT in Q4 FY26; Q1 FY27 guided at about 170 KT.
Midwest premium at about $380/t due to 50% US tariffs; Japan premium up on supply tightness and freight. Domestic vs export realisation gap narrowed; exports may be slightly higher in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Does Q4 copper EBITDA reflect the full sulfuric acid price surge, and how sustainable is the INR900 crore run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 expected in the same range given high sulfuric acid, but management guided INR600-700 crore per quarter for Q2 and Q3 and cautioned that Hormuz reopening could correct sulfur prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the India and consolidated capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: India FY27 capex about INR12,000 crore, rising to INR15,000-17,000 crore in the following year; Novelis FY27 capex $2.3-2.4 billion, falling sharply in FY28 after Bay Minette. Consolidated capex expected to be lower than current levels; FY28 detail deferred to Q3/Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt breakdown and peak?
qa_highlights.answer: India gross debt INR12,200 crore, cash INR18,000 crore (net cash INR6,000 crore). Novelis gross debt INR75,000 crore, cash INR11,000 crore (net debt INR63,000 crore). Consolidated net debt peak INR80,000-90,000 crore over the next 2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is $600/t Novelis EBITDA assuming current scrap spreads and start-up costs?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management does not assume current spreads or metal prices; start-up costs sit below EBITDA. The $600/t target is seen as sustainable, not reliant on current tailwinds.

qa_highlights.question: How do coal captive mines change costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Chakla and Bandha expected at similar cost to market coal; Meenakshi substantially lower. Captive mines expected to flatten the cost curve over 15-20 years; meaningful captive volumes only from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will Novelis avoid shipping to Canada given tariffs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is mitigating tariffs by using US cold mill capacity, including additional capacity secured at Logan; Kingston (Ontario) mill longer-term planning still pending.

risks_watch: Oswego hot mill restart timing and the resulting Novelis volume recovery in Q1 FY27.
Tariff exposure (Midwest premium, US-Canada flows) and possible relief from governments.
Input cost inflation: Q1 FY27 cost guided about 5% higher, driven by furnace oil; CP coke and pitch also rising.
Sulfuric acid and TC/RC normalisation could reduce copper EBITDA from the current run-rate if Hormuz reopens.
Captive coal ramp-up delays (Bandha high strip ratio) and Aditya smelter timelines.
Net debt rising toward INR80,000-90,000 crore; net leverage target around 2x.
Battery-grade copper foil and battery demand in India slower than expected.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India operations and cost leadership, and on Novelis recovery in FY27, but cautious on near-term macro, sulfuric acid normalisation and copper beyond Q1. Management declined to guide copper EBITDA beyond Q1 and gave ranges rather than firm figures on some capex and start-up costs.
key_quotes: Our quarterly copper EBITDA stood at a record INR907 crores, up 48% year-on-year on account of better realization in byproducts and operational efficiencies.

So, I think that Q1, to be fair, will also be in the same range because sulfuric prices are high. But I'm not going to stick my neck out to Q2 and Q3. I would still go back to the 600, 700 per quarter there.
So consolidated net debt peak should be between INR80,000 crores and INR90,000 crores over the next 2 years.
We have not factored in current scrap spreads. I mean these current scrap spreads and the current scrap market conditions; we take it as not sustainable.
So, I think that Novelis is heading to a recovery year in FY 27.

growth.why: Management expects Novelis headwinds to substantially recover in FY27 (Oswego hot mill restart in weeks, Bay Minette commercial coils in FY28) and copper EBITDA guided at INR600-700 crore per quarter for Q2-Q3 FY27, with aluminium deficit of 1.5 Mt for CY26 supporting prices; no revenue growth % guided and capacity timelines are mostly multi-quarter.
